## The y = mx + c splash names six gradients, and Post under a post is a tile

**Asked for as *"refine the gradiant animation. post should be a tile too."*** (5 October). "The
gradient animation" is `#splash-mxc`, the y = mx + c loading screen. No other splash shows a
gradient, and the only animated CSS gradients are glows. "Post" is the comment composer's button
under every post on the feed.

### The gradient splash (`#splash-mxc`, now generated by `tools/mxc.py`)

These faults were measured on the page before anything was changed:

- **The line ran off the axes.** It was a full-width bar turned 26° about a point near the left of
  its box. Its right end rose past the top of the axes, and nothing clipped it.
- **It had two gradients, and neither was named.** It rocked between `rotate(-26deg)` and
  `rotate(14deg)`, which is m ≈ 0.49 and −0.25. No number appeared anywhere, and nothing showed a
  rise or a run.
- **The pivot and the dot were two places.** The bar turned about `1.6rem 50%` of a 3px box. The dot
  was a .55rem disc with its own margins. They sat 0.2px and 0.4px apart, set by two sets of numbers
  that could each be edited alone.
- **The axes were cream written out as `rgb(244 241 232 / .28)`**, the literal CLAUDE.md forbids.

What it does now:

- **The axes have arrowheads and sit on a faint unit grid.** The plot is centred in its box. The x
  label sits past the arrow's tip, outside the clip. Every line with m between −1 and 0 cuts the
  x-axis somewhere from x = 1 to the edge, so any place beside the axis gets crossed. The first
  draw put the x above the axis, and m = −0.3 ran through it.
- **The line always goes through (0, c).** It is drawn along x through (0,0), then carried and
  turned with `translate(P) rotate(-θ)`. P is the same string in every keyframe, so the browser
  never interpolates it, and the line goes through (0, c) at every frame by construction. A
  clipPath on a still parent keeps the line inside the plot.
- **It stops at m = −1, −½, 0, ½, 1, 2**, which covers falling, flat, rising and steep. Each stop
  is held for 10.5% of a 9s loop, about 0.95s. A step between stops takes 5.4%, and the swing back
  from 2 to −1 takes 10%. Everything uses cosine easing, and the swing ends where 0% starts.
- **A rise-over-run triangle rides on the line.** The run is one grid square from (0, c). The
  triangle is a unit right triangle stretched upright by m, and it flips below the run when m is
  negative. The rise is drawn two units long and shrunk by m/2. Drawing it long and shrinking it,
  rather than stretching a short line, avoids the smear that `tools/cent.py` records. The run is
  labelled 1 and the rise is labelled with its value. Under the drawing, **"m = rise ÷ run = …"**
  shows the same value, and the two share one `@keyframes`, so they change in step. A number fades
  in over the last quarter of the move that arrives at its stop and fades out over the first
  quarter of the move that leaves. During the middle of a move no number is up, so no number is
  ever wrong for the line it sits under.
- **c is written on its own point.** The orange dot at (0, c) carries the letter c. A line that
  turns about a point passes close to every place around that point, but never across the point
  itself. Any label beside the dot gets crossed at one of the six stops. At m = 0, a label anywhere
  at height c is crossed.
- **Under the drawing, the half is a built fraction, one over two.** Cascadia's ½ glyph is sized to
  fit one character cell. At the caption's size on a 320 screen at 1x, its digits were about four
  pixels tall, the smallest type on the splash for the number the splash is about. Inside the
  drawing the glyph stays, set at 10 units.
- Only transform and opacity animate. The colours belong to this splash (`--mx-line`, `--mx-m`,
  `--mx-c`), and the axes use `--paper` at an opacity. **Under reduced motion it shows one still: m
  = 2, the triangle at its tallest, and c marked.** `.mx-line` came out of the shared
  reduced-motion list in style.css. That list's `transform: none` would have laid the line flat at
  m = 0 under the m = 2 numbers.

**The check:** `check-splash-loops.js` now covers `mxc`. The generic rules apply: one clock,
infinite, transform and opacity only, no seam, reduced motion off, and centred on the axes and
arrows. On top of those, `mxcOwn_` re-derives the picture from the keyframes:

- The dot is on the y-axis and above the x-axis.
- One grid square is one unit, and the run is one square long.
- The line, the triangle and the rise are carried to (0, c) and to (1, c) in every keyframe.
- At every stop, half-way between stops, and every 0.2%, the triangle's corner and the rise's top
  are one point on the line. The worst gap is 0.097 units.
- Each value is fully up only while the line, triangle and rise all equal it, for at least 8% of
  the loop, and two values are never up together.
- Each rise label says the caption's value, beside the middle of its rise.
- No label is crossed or touched by the line, the rise, the run or an axis while it shows. Labels
  are measured as mono-face boxes against strokes of their real width.
- The loop is 8 to 10s.
- The still shows exactly one value, and everything in it agrees with that value.

17 mutations each turned it red for their own reason:

- the pivot off (0, c)
- the triangle at the wrong m
- a duplicate value
- a wrong unique value
- a rise label that disagrees with the caption
- a label moved onto the line
- the "1" moved onto the run
- the y label moved into the sweep
- the dot moved off the axis
- a run 1.5 squares long
- the clip removed
- the still with two values up
- two values up at once
- a value up mid-turn
- the seam
- reduced motion leaving the triangle moving
- a 12s loop

### Post is a tile

- The comment composer's `Post` button is now `tile_({ icon: 'send', label: 'Post', note: 'your
  comment', act: 'cmt-add', cls: 'cmt-go', data: { id } })`. It uses the paper aeroplane, which
  `tiles.js` keeps for sending. The name it is found by, `cmt-go`, and the post's id stay. It has
  the same plate as Share, Edit and Put it up in the row above. **Nothing else in that composer was
  an action.** The box holds the words being written. The rest of the composer is `.cmt-said`, the
  line where the server's refusal is shown.
- **The handler used to write "Posting…" into the control and then restore its old text.** On a tile
  that wipes the paper aeroplane and restores an empty string, so after the first comment the tile
  is blank for good. It now uses `.tile.is-busy`, the spinning ring in place of the mark, which is
  what `send_` does for tiles. The `.cmt-form .btn.cmt-go` rule went with the button.
- **The check:** a new check-flow journey, *"Post under a post is a tile, and a comment keeps its
  mark through the wait"*. It asks:
  - that every control in the composer is a tile and there is one of them, `cmt-add` on the post's
    own id, carrying the aeroplane, named "Post…"
  - that an empty box posts nothing
  - that while it waits the tile is busy and disabled with its mark still in it
  - that a refusal gives the mark back, puts the server's sentence under the box and leaves the
    tile not busy
  - that a comment that goes through posts `addComment` with the words
  
  Eight mutations each turned it red: the old button, the old text swap, no ring, a ring never
  cleared, `cmt-go` dropped, a speech bubble instead of the aeroplane, the wrong post id, and a
  second button in the composer. `check/press.js` keeps `cmt-add` as a quiet press on an empty
  box, and its reason now names the tile.

**For the owner to confirm:**

1. **CLAUDE.md files "the composer" under FORMS, which keep buttons.** Post is a tile on the owner's
   word. This applies to the comment box under a post, which is a thing's own row and not a sheet.
   That line in CLAUDE.md wants bringing into step at the merge.
2. **Two other "Post it" buttons are still buttons.** One is on the camera card (`cam-post`, in the
   Again / Add another / Save a copy row). The other is in the new-post sheet (`post-send`, a form
   with a link box, caption, place and poll). If "post" meant the camera's, say so and it is the
   same change.
3. **A comment's own `Remove` stays an underlined word in its time line.** It is on the comment,
   not the composer, and a bin tile on every line of an admin's thread is a lot of tiles.
4. **The splash's halves:** the glyph ½ inside the drawing and a stacked 1 over 2 in the caption.
   Decimals (0.5) read even more plainly, if the owner prefers them.

No sheet columns and no backend change. The site deploys by `git push`.
